request.query: Does UPI OC 226A remove the device security validations and customer consent requirements?

Yours faithfully, SD/- Sourabh Tomar Deputy Chief UPI Product

request.query: Compare the documented requirements and conditions in circulars 226A and 226. Explain what differs, retaining each source attribution.

claims.text: Circular 226A (issued 03rd July 2026) revises the per-transaction limit for On-Device Biometric Authentication in UPI from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000, effective 07th August 2026.

Circular 226 (issued 07th October 2025) introduced On-Device Biometric Authentication as an additional option in lieu of UPI PIN, initially available for transactions up to ₹5,000 with a directive to review the limit based on performance.
Circular 226A retains the requirement that all existing validations, compliance requirements, specifications, and regulatory guidelines shall continue to remain fully applicable.

Circular 226 requires UPI Applications / PSP Banks to perform device compatibility validations and security validations including restricting usage on rooted or jail-broken devices before authentication.
Circular 226 mandates that Issuer Banks, PSP Banks, and UPI Applications ensure explicit customer consent is obtained with the ability to opt out at any time for biometric authentication.
Circular 226 requires a fresh consent after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions.
Circular 226 mandates that Issuer Banks disable the biometric method for all UPI Applications in case of changes or resets to the UPI PIN until a fresh consent is captured.
Circular 226 requires UPI Applications / PSP Banks to ensure key rotation operation is undertaken before one year of biometric enablement.

Circular 226 mandates that UPI Applications / PSP Banks mark the customer as inactive for this method if no transactions are performed within ninety days through this method, activated only upon customer confirmation.

sources.text: NPCI/UPI/OC-226A/2026-27 — 03rd July 2026 To, All UPI Member Issuer Banks, PSP Banks and UPI Applications Dear Sir/Madam, **Subject: Enhancement of Transaction Limit for On-Device Biometric Authentication in UPI** Reference is drawn to NPCI circular NPCI/UPI/OC-226/2025-26 dated 07th October 2025, wherein On-Device Biometric Authentication (Fingerprint, Face, etc) was introduced as an additional option for authentication in lieu of UPI PIN. In view of increasing adoption in the ecosystem, it has been decided to revise the per-transaction limit for On-Device Biometric Authentication (fingerprint, face, etc.) in UPI is hereby enhanced from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000, effective 07th August 2026. Issuer Banks, PSP Banks and UPI Applications to ensure adequate customer communication regarding the updated limit. All existing validations, compliance requirements, specifications, and regulatory guidelines shall continue to remain fully applicable, and participants are required to ensure adherence. Yours faithfully, SD/- Sourabh Tomar Deputy Chief UPI Product

claims.text: Circular 226A (issued 03rd July 2026) revises the per-transaction limit for On-Device Biometric Authentication in UPI from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000, effective 07th August 2026.

Circular 226 (issued 07th October 2025) introduced On-Device Biometric Authentication as an additional option in lieu of UPI PIN, initially available for transactions up to ₹5,000 with a directive to review the limit based on performance.
Circular 226A retains the requirement that all existing validations, compliance requirements, specifications, and regulatory guidelines shall continue to remain fully applicable.

Circular 226 requires UPI Applications / PSP Banks to perform device compatibility validations and security validations including restricting usage on rooted or jail-broken devices before authentication.
Circular 226 mandates that Issuer Banks, PSP Banks, and UPI Applications ensure explicit customer consent is obtained with the ability to opt out at any time for biometric authentication.
Circular 226 requires a fresh consent after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions.
Circular 226 mandates that Issuer Banks disable the biometric method for all UPI Applications in case of changes or resets to the UPI PIN until a fresh consent is captured.
Circular 226 requires UPI Applications / PSP Banks to ensure key rotation operation is undertaken before one year of biometric enablement.

Circular 226 mandates that UPI Applications / PSP Banks mark the customer as inactive for this method if no transactions are performed within ninety days through this method, activated only upon customer confirmation.

claims.text: Member banks are advised to use the Deemed Debit report and raw files for reconciliation purposes and necessary actions.

Remitter and Acquirer banks are advised to perform three (3) way reconciliation for non-financial requests (create, update, revoke) and financial requests (execution) using both Mandate raw file and transaction raw file including the Deemed Debit file.

sources.text: NPCI e Lpe hi at NATIONALPAYMENTSCORPORATIONOFINDIA NPCI/UPI/OCNo.128/2021-22 14th December, 2021 To All Members-Unified Payment Interface DearMadam/Sir, Subiect: Extension of additional response codes under Deemed Debit for mandate execution Mandate transactions functions with the premise that any mandate that is created successfully must also be executed successfully. To reduce the remitter end declines in case of the mandates execution including use case of [POs, we have developed the functionality of Deemed Debit (DD) for financial mandate execution which was introduced through UPI OC 88 dated 14th May, 2020 - Migration of "UP] - RGCS" system to “UPI Real Time Clearing & Settlement" (URCS) system w.e.f. 25th May 2020 wherein a few response codes under mandate execution was considered as Deemed Debit. Basis the ecosystem feedback, we have now extended the scope of Deemed Debit at the remitter side further wherein any declines at the remitter end shall be considered as Deemed Debit. Only in case if the remitter bank declines the transaction with the below mentioned response codes the transaction shall be considered as failure and shall not be treated as Deemed Debit. request.query: Does the 10 lakh cumulative Capital Market figure in UPI OC 185B make a single IPO mandate limit 10 lakh?

claims.text: The table in UPI OC 185B (Annexure I) lists a 'Cumulative Limits (24 hrs)' of ₹10 Lakh for the Capital Market category but does not state that this figure sets the per-mandate limit for a single IPO.

Earlier circular OC 127 established a specific per-transaction ceiling of Rs 5 Lakh for Retail Direct Scheme and UPI-based ASBA IPO transactions, distinguishing this mandate limit from other categories.

The ₹10 lakh cumulative limit in OC 185B applies to the total value of Capital Market transactions within a 24-hour period and does not alter the per-mandate ceiling for a single IPO transaction, which remains governed by Circular 127 at ₹5 lakh.

claims.text: Circular 185A (issued 24 August 2024) enhanced the per transaction limit to Rs 5 lakh specifically for entities under categories aligned to tax payments, which were restricted to MCC-9311.

Circular 185A (issued 24 August 2024) limited the enhanced limit applicability strictly to 'Verified Merchants' and required acquiring entities to ensure MCC-9311 classification adheres only to tax payments.
Circular 185A (issued 24 August 2024) mandated compliance by 15 September 2024 and included specific categories such as Hospitals, Educational Services, IPO & G Sec, and Retail Direct Scheme.

Circular 185B (issued 28 August 2025) expanded the scope of higher per transaction limits to additional categories beyond tax payments, including Capital Market, Insurance, Government e-Market Place, Travel, Credit Card Bill Payments, Collections, Business/Merchant, Jewellery, FX Retail use case, and Digital Account Opening.

Circular 185B (issued 28 August 2025) retained the requirement that enhanced limits apply only to merchants categorized as 'Verified Merchant' and required acquiring member banks to ensure compliance with NPCI UPI guidelines.
Circular 185B (issued 28 August 2025) extended the compliance deadline to 15 September 2025 and explicitly stated that P2P per transaction limits shall continue as per extant guidelines.

claims.text: Under OC 223 (circular number 223), the 'Port Mandate' feature must be strictly user-driven only from the mandate details page fetched with 'View Mandate', and no inducements or automated prompts may be employed to solicit portability.

The rules in OC 223 prohibit utilizing mandate details obtained through the 'view mandate' for any other purpose, implying that automatic porting without explicit user action is not permitted.

request.query: On FASTag auto-replenishment, can the issuer omit the message after a debit because advance notice is exempt under RBI rules?

claims.text: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) explicitly exempts auto-replenishment of NETC FASTag and RuPay NCMC from the requirement to send a Pre-Debit Notification (PDN) at least 24 hours prior to debit.

This exemption is codified in RBI Circular RBI/2024-25/64 CO.DPSS.POLC.No.S528/02-14-003/2024-25 issued on 22 August 2024, which permits auto-replenishment without the standard 24-hour prior notification.

flagged_claims.text: Consequently, issuers are permitted to omit the pre-debit message after a debit occurs for these specific auto-replenishment transactions because advance notice is exempt under RBI rules.
review_reasons: The cited notification rule concerns a different event phase. A pre-transaction exemption does not establish a post-transaction exemption, or vice versa.

request.query: Compare the documented requirements and conditions in circulars 141 and 76. Explain what differs, retaining each source attribution.

claims.text: Circular 141 requires Acquirers to tag P2P Lending platforms specifically under MCC 7408 only.
Circular 141 mandates that Online gaming (MCC 5816) be allowed via Push payment and In-App intent only for Users with Android-based devices, excluding other initiation modes.
Circular 141 classifies Gift/Prepaid cards acting as prepaid instruments as MCC 6540.

Circular 141 restricts Rent payments (MCC 6513) and all Gift/Prepaid Cards to Push payment (mode 00 with sub type 'Pay') and In-App intent (modes 04 & 05), referencing an addendum dated 2nd April 2025.

Circular 141 requires Acquirers to ensure visibility of the Ultimate Beneficiary and mandates that each Ultimate Beneficiary have a unique UPI ID for specific MCCs including P2P Lending, Digital Goods, Wallet top up, and Real Estate Agents.
Circular 141 states it is not applicable for Mandate Transactions (One time and Recurring Mandates).

Circular 141 reiterates that Acquirers are responsible for correct assignment of MCCs and compliance to guidelines for aggregators/sub-merchants, with liability for fraud resting with the respective Acquirer.
Circular 141 advises UPI Members to adhere to the P2P inward credit limit as defined by NPCI in a separate circular dated 4th September 2024.

Circular 76 allows Online merchants (including verified merchants) to generate collect requests greater than Rs 2,000 only if the request is system generated or customer initiated, not performed manually by the merchant.
Circular 76 assigns full liability to the Payee PSP Bank for any fraudulent collect or transaction initiated via Share Intent Link and Pay QR Share and Pay.

Circular 76 decides to disable all Wallet loads (MCC 6540) through Collect requests, allowing wallet top-ups only through limited 'Pay' modes of UPI excluding Share Intent Link and Pay & QR Share and Pay.
Circular 76 requires Member Banks to comply with its provisions by 20th November, 2019.

Circular 226A retains the requirement that all existing validations, compliance requirements, specifications, and regulatory guidelines shall continue to remain fully applicable.

Circular 226 requires UPI Applications / PSP Banks to perform device compatibility validations and security validations including restricting usage on rooted or jail-broken devices before authentication.
Circular 226 mandates that Issuer Banks, PSP Banks, and UPI Applications ensure explicit customer consent is obtained with the ability to opt out at any time for biometric authentication.
Circular 226 requires a fresh consent after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions.
Circular 226 mandates that Issuer Banks disable the biometric method for all UPI Applications in case of changes or resets to the UPI PIN until a fresh consent is captured.
Circular 226 requires UPI Applications / PSP Banks to ensure key rotation operation is undertaken before one year of biometric enablement.

Circular 226 mandates that UPI Applications / PSP Banks mark the customer as inactive for this method if no transactions are performed within ninety days through this method, activated only upon customer confirmation.

In view of increasing adoption in the ecosystem, it has been decided to revise the per-transaction limit for On-Device Biometric Authentication (fingerprint, face, etc.) in UPI is hereby enhanced from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000, effective 07th August 2026. Issuer Banks, PSP Banks and UPI Applications to ensure adequate customer communication regarding the updated limit. All existing validations, compliance requirements, specifications, and regulatory guidelines shall continue to remain fully applicable, and participants are required to ensure adherence. Yours faithfully, SD/- Sourabh Tomar Deputy Chief UPI Product

claims.text: Circular 226A (issued 03rd July 2026) revises the per-transaction limit for On-Device Biometric Authentication in UPI from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000, effective 07th August 2026.

Circular 226 (issued 07th October 2025) introduced On-Device Biometric Authentication as an additional option in lieu of UPI PIN, initially available for transactions up to ₹5,000 with a directive to review the limit based on performance.
Circular 226A retains the requirement that all existing validations, compliance requirements, specifications, and regulatory guidelines shall continue to remain fully applicable.

Circular 226 requires UPI Applications / PSP Banks to perform device compatibility validations and security validations including restricting usage on rooted or jail-broken devices before authentication.
Circular 226 mandates that Issuer Banks, PSP Banks, and UPI Applications ensure explicit customer consent is obtained with the ability to opt out at any time for biometric authentication.
Circular 226 requires a fresh consent after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions.
Circular 226 mandates that Issuer Banks disable the biometric method for all UPI Applications in case of changes or resets to the UPI PIN until a fresh consent is captured.
Circular 226 requires UPI Applications / PSP Banks to ensure key rotation operation is undertaken before one year of biometric enablement.

Circular 226 mandates that UPI Applications / PSP Banks mark the customer as inactive for this method if no transactions are performed within ninety days through this method, activated only upon customer confirmation.

claims.text: The table in UPI OC 185B (Annexure I) lists a 'Cumulative Limits (24 hrs)' of ₹10 Lakh for the Capital Market category but does not state that this figure sets the per-mandate limit for a single IPO.

Earlier circular OC 127 established a specific per-transaction ceiling of Rs 5 Lakh for Retail Direct Scheme and UPI-based ASBA IPO transactions, distinguishing this mandate limit from other categories.
The cumulative limit column in OC 185B is a separate measure that does not by itself change the per-mandate ceiling for a single IPO transaction.

request.query: Compare the documented requirements and conditions in circulars 185B and 185A. Explain what differs, retaining each source attribution.

claims.text: Circular 185A (issued 24 August 2024) enhanced the per transaction limit to Rs 5 lakh specifically for entities under categories aligned to tax payments, which were restricted to MCC-9311.

Circular 185A (issued 24 August 2024) limited the enhanced limit applicability strictly to 'Verified Merchants' and required acquiring entities to ensure MCC-9311 classification adheres only to tax payments.
Circular 185A (issued 24 August 2024) mandated compliance by 15 September 2024 and included specific categories such as Hospitals, Educational Services, IPO & G Sec, and Retail Direct Scheme.

Circular 185B (issued 28 August 2025) expanded the scope of higher per transaction limits to additional categories beyond tax payments, including Capital Market, Insurance, Government e-Market Place, Travel, Credit Card Bill Payments, Collections, Business/Merchant, Jewellery, FX Retail use case, and Digital Account Opening.

Circular 185B (issued 28 August 2025) retained the requirement that enhanced limits apply only to merchants categorized as 'Verified Merchant' and required acquiring member banks to ensure compliance with NPCI UPI guidelines.
Circular 185B (issued 28 August 2025) extended the compliance deadline to 15 September 2025 and explicitly stated that P2P per transaction limits shall continue as per extant guidelines.

claims.text: Circular 185A (issued 24 August 2024) enhanced the per transaction limit to Rs 5 lakh specifically for entities under categories aligned to tax payments, which were restricted to MCC-9311.

Circular 185A (issued 24 August 2024) limited the enhanced limit applicability strictly to 'Verified Merchants' and required acquiring entities to ensure MCC-9311 classification adheres only to tax payments.
Circular 185A (issued 24 August 2024) mandated compliance by 15 September 2024 and included specific categories such as Hospitals, Educational Services, IPO & G Sec, and Retail Direct Scheme.

Circular 185B (issued 28 August 2025) expanded the scope of higher per transaction limits to additional categories beyond tax payments, including Capital Market, Insurance, Government e-Market Place, Travel, Credit Card Bill Payments, Collections, Business/Merchant, Jewellery, FX Retail use case, and Digital Account Opening.

Circular 185B (issued 28 August 2025) retained the requirement that enhanced limits apply only to merchants categorized as 'Verified Merchant' and required acquiring member banks to ensure compliance with NPCI UPI guidelines.
Circular 185B (issued 28 August 2025) extended the compliance deadline to 15 September 2025 and explicitly stated that P2P per transaction limits shall continue as per extant guidelines.

claims.text: Under OC 223 (circular number 223), the 'Port Mandate' feature must be strictly user-driven only from the mandate details page fetched with 'View Mandate', and no inducements or automated prompts may be employed to solicit portability.

OC 223 explicitly states that Payer PSPs and UPI apps shall ensure lifecycle management, including viewing and porting of user's UPI Autopay mandates on the respective app only under the 'Manage Bank accounts' or the dedicated 'UPI Autopay' section.
The rules in OC 223 prohibit utilizing mandate details obtained through the 'view mandate' for any other purpose, implying that automatic porting without explicit user action is not permitted.

findings.reason: The answer claims that OC 223 prohibits automatic porting and mandates user-driven actions (S1.1), but it simultaneously asserts that OC 223 allows viewing mandates in 'any app of their choice' and porting from one app to another (S4.1). While S4.1 describes the *capability* for users to port, S1.1 explicitly restricts the *mechanism* to a specific page ('mandate details page fetched with View Mandate') and forbids 'automated prompts'. The answer's support_status of 'automated_supported' contradicts the explicit prohibition in S1.1 against 'No inducements... nudges, alerts' which implies automation is not permitted. The distinction between user-initiated capability (S4.1) and prohibited automated solicitation (S1.1) is blurred in the answer's conclusion that rules 'mean' apps may automatically port.

request.query: Compare the documented requirements and conditions in circulars 141 and 76. Explain what differs, retaining each source attribution.

claims.text: Circular 141 requires Acquirers to tag P2P Lending platforms specifically under MCC 7408 only.
Circular 141 mandates that Online gaming (MCC 5816) be allowed via Push payment and In-App intent only for Users with Android-based devices, excluding other initiation modes.
Circular 141 classifies Gift/Prepaid cards acting as prepaid instruments as MCC 6540.

Circular 141 restricts Rent payments (MCC 6513) and all Gift/Prepaid Cards to Push payment (mode 00 with sub type 'Pay') and In-App intent (modes 04 & 05), referencing an addendum dated 2nd April 2025.

Circular 141 requires Acquirers to ensure visibility of the Ultimate Beneficiary and mandates that each Ultimate Beneficiary have a unique UPI ID for specific MCCs including P2P Lending, Digital Goods, Wallet top up, and Real Estate Agents.
Circular 141 states it is not applicable for Mandate Transactions (One time and Recurring Mandates).

Circular 141 reiterates that Acquirers are responsible for correct assignment of MCCs and compliance to guidelines for aggregators/sub-merchants, with liability for fraud resting with the respective Acquirer.
Circular 141 advises UPI Members to adhere to the P2P inward credit limit as defined by NPCI in a separate circular dated 4th September 2024.

Circular 76 allows Online merchants (including verified merchants) to generate collect requests greater than Rs 2,000 only if the request is system generated or customer initiated, not performed manually by the merchant.
Circular 76 assigns full liability to the Payee PSP Bank for any fraudulent collect or transaction initiated via Share Intent Link and Pay QR Share and Pay.

Circular 76 decides to disable all Wallet loads (MCC 6540) through Collect requests, allowing wallet top-ups only through limited 'Pay' modes of UPI excluding Share Intent Link and Pay & QR Share and Pay.
Circular 76 requires Member Banks to comply with its provisions by 20th November, 2019.
